name: Pale Butter
lede: Pale Butter is a soft, pale yellow named for the food, close to the pale rind of a fresh stick of dairy butter.

sections.title: A food name
sections.body:
The name comes from the xkcd color survey of 2010, where volunteers typed in names for a grid of random swatches, and "pale butter" was common enough to make the final list [1]. No book in our library records the phrase before that, so its coinage is undocumented here [1].

The ISCC-NBS system classifies the nearest block as a light greenish yellow, 4.7 units away by CIEDE2000, and the Munsell notation for that block runs close to 2.5Y in hue [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[light-green-yellow]], [[light-chalcedony-yellow]], [[lemon-yellow-crayola]] and [[pastel-yellow]], at 2.9, 3.2, 3.8 and 3.9 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for Pale Butter in just 8 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. Émile Bernard's *La Moisson* (1888) carries the most of it, covering about 20 per cent of the canvas [2]. Where it appears, it plays the brightest of a painting's six sampled colors every time, never a shadow or a mid tone [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so read the hex as a screen approximation, not a pigment match [2].
